rules.rule_name: Program Initialization and File Opening
rules.rule_description: At program startup, the system captures and displays the current processing date, then opens both the Root Segment File (INFILE1) and the Child Segment File (INFILE2) required for the IMS database load.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
1:Program Initialization
Capture current date & display it
Open Root Segment File and Child Segment File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The PAUDBLOD program has been started and both the Root Segment File (INFILE1) and the Child Segment File (INFILE2) are available for processing
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initializes by capturing the current date and attempting to open both input files
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current processing date is captured and displayed; both the Root Segment File and the Child Segment File are successfully opened for reading, and processing continues to the root segment loading phase

rules.rule_name: File Open Failure Terminates Program
rules.rule_description: If either the Root Segment File or the Child Segment File cannot be opened successfully at program startup, the program must terminate immediately with an error.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
File Open
Successful?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The PAUDBLOD program has been started and is attempting to open the Root Segment File (INFILE1) or the Child Segment File (INFILE2)
acceptance_criteria.When: Either file fails to open successfully (file open status is not blank or '00')
acceptance_criteria.Then: An error message is displayed identifying which file failed to open along with its error status, and the program terminates abnormally with return code 16

rules.rule_name: Sequential Reading of Root Segment Records
rules.rule_description: The program reads all Pending Authorization Summary records sequentially from the Root Segment File one at a time, continuing until all records have been processed and end-of-file is reached.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2:Read Root
Segment Records
End of File?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Root Segment File (INFILE1) has been successfully opened and contains Pending Authorization Summary records
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reads each record sequentially from the Root Segment File
acceptance_criteria.Then: Each successfully read record is moved into the PENDING-AUTH-SUMMARY structure and passed for insertion into the IMS database; when end-of-file is reached, the program transitions to processing the Child Segment File

rules.rule_name: Insert Pending Authorization Summary as Root Segment
rules.rule_description: Each Pending Authorization Summary record read from the Root Segment File is inserted into the IMS database as a root segment (PAUTSUM0) using an unqualified SSA insert call.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
3:Insert Root Segment into Database
Insert root summary segment PAUTSUM0
into IMS Database

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Summary record has been successfully read from the Root Segment File and loaded into the PENDING-AUTH-SUMMARY structure
acceptance_criteria.When: The program performs an IMS INSERT (ISRT) call using the root unqualified SSA to insert the record as a PAUTSUM0 root segment in the IMS database
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Pending Authorization Summary record is inserted as a root segment into the IMS database, and the program logs a success message and continues reading the next root record

rules.rule_name: Handle Successful Root Segment Insert
rules.rule_description: When a Pending Authorization Summary root segment is successfully inserted into the IMS database, the program logs the success and continues processing the next root record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Insert
Successful?

acceptance_criteria.Given: An IMS INSERT call has been made for a Pending Authorization Summary root segment (PAUTSUM0)
acceptance_criteria.When: The IMS INSERT call returns a successful status (blank status code)
acceptance_criteria.Then: A success message 'ROOT INSERT SUCCESS' is displayed and the program continues to read and process the next root segment record from the Root Segment File

rules.rule_name: Handle Duplicate Root Segment
rules.rule_description: If a Pending Authorization Summary record being inserted already exists in the IMS database, the duplicate is acknowledged and processing continues without error.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4:Handle Duplicate Root Segment
Root segment already exists in DB
Log message and continue

acceptance_criteria.Given: An IMS INSERT call has been made for a Pending Authorization Summary root segment (PAUTSUM0)
acceptance_criteria.When: The IMS INSERT call returns a duplicate key status (status code 'II'), indicating the root segment already exists in the database
acceptance_criteria.Then: A message 'ROOT SEGMENT ALREADY IN DB' is displayed, no error is raised, and the program continues to read and process the next root segment record from the Root Segment File

rules.rule_name: Handle Root Segment Insert Failure
rules.rule_description: If a Pending Authorization Summary root segment insert fails for any reason other than a duplicate, the program logs the failure and terminates immediately.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
5:Handle Root Segment Insert Failure
Log failure status
Terminate program with error

acceptance_criteria.Given: An IMS INSERT call has been made for a Pending Authorization Summary root segment (PAUTSUM0)
acceptance_criteria.When: The IMS INSERT call returns a status that is neither successful (blank) nor a duplicate key ('II'), indicating an unexpected insert failure
acceptance_criteria.Then: A failure message 'ROOT INSERT FAILED' along with the IMS status code is displayed, and the program terminates abnormally with return code 16

rules.rule_name: Sequential Reading of Child Segment Records
rules.rule_description: After all root segments have been loaded, the program reads all Pending Authorization Detail records sequentially from the Child Segment File one at a time, continuing until all records have been processed and end-of-file is reached.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
3:Read Child
Segment Records
End of File?

acceptance_criteria.Given: All root segment records have been fully processed and the Child Segment File (INFILE2) has been successfully opened and contains Pending Authorization Detail records
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reads each record sequentially from the Child Segment File
acceptance_criteria.Then: Each successfully read record is evaluated for a valid numeric Account ID; when end-of-file is reached, the program transitions to the file close phase

rules.rule_name: Validate Child Segment Account ID is Numeric
rules.rule_description: Before processing a child segment record, the Account ID (ROOT-SEG-KEY) must be validated as numeric. Records with non-numeric Account IDs are silently skipped without error.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7:Validate Child
Segment Key
Is Account ID Numeric?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail record has been successfully read from the Child Segment File (INFILE2)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program evaluates whether the ROOT-SEG-KEY (Account ID) field in the child record contains a valid numeric value
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Account ID is numeric, the record is passed for parent lookup and child insertion; if the Account ID is not numeric, the record is silently skipped and the program reads the next child record without logging any error or warning

rules.rule_name: Locate Parent Root Segment Before Child Insert
rules.rule_description: Before inserting a Pending Authorization Detail child segment, the program must verify that the corresponding parent Pending Authorization Summary root segment exists in the IMS database by performing a qualified Get Unique lookup using the Account ID.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8:Locate Parent Root Segment
Perform qualified GU call using Account ID
to find parent root segment PAUTSUM0

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail record with a valid numeric Account ID has been read from the Child Segment File, and the Account ID has been moved to the qualified SSA key value
acceptance_criteria.When: The program performs an IMS GET UNIQUE (GU) call using the qualified root SSA with the Account ID to locate the parent PAUTSUM0 root segment in the IMS database
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the parent root segment is found (blank status), the program proceeds to insert the child segment; if the parent is not found or the lookup fails, the program logs the failure and terminates abnormally

rules.rule_name: Handle Root Segment Not Found for Child Insert
rules.rule_description: If the parent Pending Authorization Summary root segment cannot be located in the IMS database when attempting to insert a child detail record, the program logs the failure details and terminates immediately.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
9:Handle Root Segment Not Found for Child
Log failure status and key feedback area
Terminate program with error

acceptance_criteria.Given: An IMS GET UNIQUE (GU) call has been made to locate the parent PAUTSUM0 root segment using the Account ID from the child record
acceptance_criteria.When: The GU call returns a status that is not successful (not blank), indicating the parent root segment was not found or the lookup failed
acceptance_criteria.Then: A failure message 'ROOT GU CALL FAIL' along with the IMS status code and the key feedback area (PAUT-KEYFB) is displayed, and the program terminates abnormally with return code 16

rules.rule_name: Insert Pending Authorization Detail as Child Segment
rules.rule_description: After the parent root segment is confirmed to exist, the Pending Authorization Detail record is inserted into the IMS database as a child segment (PAUTDTL1) under the located parent root segment.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10:Insert Child Segment into Database
Insert child detail segment PAUTDTL1
under parent in IMS Database

acceptance_criteria.Given: The parent PAUTSUM0 root segment has been successfully located in the IMS database using the Account ID, and the child record data has been loaded into the PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS structure
acceptance_criteria.When: The program performs an IMS INSERT (ISRT) call using the child unqualified SSA to insert the record as a PAUTDTL1 child segment under the parent root segment
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Pending Authorization Detail record is inserted as a child segment under the correct parent in the IMS database, and the program logs a success message and continues reading the next child record

rules.rule_name: Handle Duplicate Child Segment
rules.rule_description: If a Pending Authorization Detail child segment being inserted already exists in the IMS database under its parent, the duplicate is acknowledged and processing continues without error.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11:Handle Duplicate Child Segment
Child segment already exists in DB
Log message and continue

acceptance_criteria.Given: An IMS INSERT call has been made for a Pending Authorization Detail child segment (PAUTDTL1) under its parent root segment
acceptance_criteria.When: The IMS INSERT call returns a duplicate key status (status code 'II'), indicating the child segment already exists under the parent in the database
acceptance_criteria.Then: A message 'CHILD SEGMENT ALREADY IN DB' is displayed, no error is raised, and the program continues to read and process the next child segment record from the Child Segment File

rules.rule_name: Handle Child Segment Insert Failure
rules.rule_description: If a Pending Authorization Detail child segment insert fails for any reason other than a duplicate, the program logs the failure details including the key feedback area and terminates immediately.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
12:Handle Child Segment Insert Failure
Log failure status and key feedback area
Terminate program with error

acceptance_criteria.Given: An IMS INSERT call has been made for a Pending Authorization Detail child segment (PAUTDTL1) under its parent root segment
acceptance_criteria.When: The IMS INSERT call returns a status that is neither successful (blank) nor a duplicate key ('II'), indicating an unexpected insert failure
acceptance_criteria.Then: A failure message 'INSERT CALL FAIL FOR CHILD' along with the IMS status code and the key feedback area (PAUT-KEYFB) is displayed, and the program terminates abnormally with return code 16

rules.rule_name: Close Input Files After Processing
rules.rule_description: After all root and child segment records have been fully processed, both input files are closed and any file close errors are logged.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
13:Close Input Files
Close Root Segment File and Child Segment File
Log any errors encountered

acceptance_criteria.Given: All records from both the Root Segment File (INFILE1) and the Child Segment File (INFILE2) have been fully processed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program closes both the Root Segment File and the Child Segment File
acceptance_criteria.Then: Both files are closed successfully; if any file fails to close, an error message identifying the file and its error status is displayed, and the program proceeds to normal completion

rules.rule_name: Abnormal Program Termination
rules.rule_description: When any critical processing failure occurs during the IMS load, the program terminates abnormally with a standardized error return code to signal failure to any calling or scheduling process.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
14:Abnormal Program Termination
Display abort message
Set return code to 16 and terminate

acceptance_criteria.Given: A critical failure has occurred during program execution, such as a file open error, a root segment insert failure, a parent segment not found condition, or a child segment insert failure
acceptance_criteria.When: The program invokes the abnormal termination routine (9999-ABEND)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message 'IMS LOAD ABENDING ...' is displayed, the program return code is set to 16 to signal abnormal termination, and the program exits immediately without further processing

rules.rule_name: Root Segments Must Be Fully Loaded Before Child Segments
rules.rule_description: The program enforces a strict sequential processing order where all Pending Authorization Summary root segments must be completely loaded into the IMS database before any Pending Authorization Detail child segments are processed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2:Read Root
Segment Records
End of File?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The PAUDBLOD program has been initialized and both input files are open
acceptance_criteria.When: The program begins its processing sequence
acceptance_criteria.Then: All records from the Root Segment File are read and inserted into the IMS database first; only after the Root Segment File is fully exhausted (end-of-file reached) does the program begin reading and processing records from the Child Segment File

rules.rule_name: Capture and Display Program Start Date
rules.rule_description: At the start of program initialization, the program captures the current calendar date and Julian date, then displays the current date to the processing log to record when the IMS load run was initiated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture Current Date and Display It

acceptance_criteria.Given: The PAUDBLOD program has been invoked and is beginning its initialization phase
acceptance_criteria.When: The program starts execution
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must capture the current calendar date and the current Julian day-of-year, display a separator line, and display today's date in the processing log before any file operations begin

rules.rule_name: Open Root Segment Input File for Processing
rules.rule_description: During initialization, the program must open the Root Segment input file (INFILE1), which contains Pending Authorization Summary records, before any root segment data can be read and loaded into the database.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Open Root Segment Input File - INFILE1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has completed capturing and displaying the current date during initialization
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Root Segment input file (INFILE1) containing Pending Authorization Summary records
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Root Segment input file must be opened successfully in read-only (INPUT) mode so that Pending Authorization Summary records can be read for database loading

rules.rule_name: Validate Successful Opening of Root Segment File
rules.rule_description: After attempting to open the Root Segment input file, the program validates whether the file was opened successfully. If the file cannot be opened, the program logs an error and terminates abnormally, preventing any further processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: INFILE1 Opened Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the Root Segment input file (INFILE1) containing Pending Authorization Summary records
acceptance_criteria.When: The file open status is evaluated — the file open is considered successful when the status is blank or '00', and unsuccessful for any other status value
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file opened successfully, the program proceeds to open the Child Segment input file; if the file failed to open, the program logs the error message 'ERROR IN OPENING INFILE1' along with the file status code, and immediately terminates abnormally with a return code of 16

rules.rule_name: Open Child Segment Input File for Processing
rules.rule_description: After successfully opening the Root Segment input file, the program must also open the Child Segment input file (INFILE2), which contains Pending Authorization Detail records, before any child segment data can be read and loaded into the database.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Open Child Segment Input File - INFILE2

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Root Segment input file (INFILE1) has been successfully opened and the program is continuing initialization
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Child Segment input file (INFILE2) containing Pending Authorization Detail records
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Child Segment input file must be opened successfully in read-only (INPUT) mode so that Pending Authorization Detail records can be read for database loading

rules.rule_name: Validate Successful Opening of Child Segment File
rules.rule_description: After attempting to open the Child Segment input file, the program validates whether the file was opened successfully. If the file cannot be opened, the program logs an error and terminates abnormally, preventing any further processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: INFILE2 Opened Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the Child Segment input file (INFILE2) containing Pending Authorization Detail records
acceptance_criteria.When: The file open status is evaluated — the file open is considered successful when the status is blank or '00', and unsuccessful for any other status value
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the file opened successfully, the program proceeds to the next phase of processing (reading Root Segment records); if the file failed to open, the program logs the error message 'ERROR IN OPENING INFILE2' along with the file status code, and immediately terminates abnormally with a return code of 16

rules.rule_name: Enforce Sequential File Opening Order During Initialization
rules.rule_description: Both the Root Segment input file and the Child Segment input file must be opened successfully and in a specific sequence — Root Segment file first, then Child Segment file — before any data loading activity can begin. Processing cannot proceed unless both files are available.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Initialization Complete
Proceed to Read Root Segment Records

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is in its initialization phase and needs to prepare for loading Pending Authorization Summary and Pending Authorization Detail records
acceptance_criteria.When: The program completes the initialization sequence
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Root Segment input file (INFILE1) must be opened first, followed by the Child Segment input file (INFILE2); only after both files are confirmed open and ready may the program proceed to read and process Root Segment records; if either file fails to open, the program must not proceed to any data loading activity

rules.rule_name: Abnormal Program Termination on Initialization Failure
rules.rule_description: If any critical failure occurs during program initialization — specifically the failure to open either input file — the program must terminate abnormally, log the termination, and signal failure to the calling process by setting a return code of 16.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

acceptance_criteria.Given: A critical failure has occurred during program initialization, such as the inability to open the Root Segment input file (INFILE1) or the Child Segment input file (INFILE2)
acceptance_criteria.When: The abnormal termination routine is invoked
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must display the message 'IMS LOAD ABENDING', set the program return code to 16 to signal a hard failure to any calling or scheduling process, and immediately stop all further processing

rules.rule_name: Sequential Reading of Pending Authorization Summary Records
rules.rule_description: Each Pending Authorization Summary record is read sequentially from the Root Segment input file one at a time, and processing continues until all records have been read.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Read Next Record
from Root Segment File INFILE1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Root Segment input file (INFILE1) has been successfully opened and contains Pending Authorization Summary records
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reads the next available record from the Root Segment input file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The record is made available for further processing as a Pending Authorization Summary record, and the program continues to read subsequent records until the end of the file is reached

rules.rule_name: Map Root Segment Record to Pending Authorization Summary
rules.rule_description: When a root segment record is successfully read from the input file, its data is mapped to the Pending Authorization Summary structure before being inserted into the database.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Move Record to
Pending Auth Summary

acceptance_criteria.Given: A record has been successfully read from the Root Segment input file (INFILE1)
acceptance_criteria.When: The record read status confirms the record is available and valid
acceptance_criteria.Then: The entire record content from INFILE1 is mapped to the Pending Authorization Summary (PENDING-AUTH-SUMMARY) data structure, making it ready for database insertion

rules.rule_name: Insert Pending Authorization Summary Record into Database
rules.rule_description: Each Pending Authorization Summary record mapped from the input file must be inserted into the IMS database as a root segment (PAUTSUM0) using an unqualified segment search argument.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Insert Root Segment PAUTSUM0
into IMS Database

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Summary record has been successfully mapped from the Root Segment input file
acceptance_criteria.When: The program invokes the IMS database insert operation for the Pending Authorization Summary segment (PAUTSUM0) using the root unqualified segment search argument
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Pending Authorization Summary record is submitted for insertion into the IMS database as a root-level segment, and the resulting insert status is captured for further evaluation

rules.rule_name: Successful Insertion of Pending Authorization Summary Record
rules.rule_description: When a Pending Authorization Summary record is successfully inserted into the database, the program logs the success and proceeds to read and process the next record from the input file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Log: Root Insert Success
Continue to Next Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: An insert operation has been performed for a Pending Authorization Summary record into the IMS database
acceptance_criteria.When: The database insert operation returns a successful status (blank/spaces status code)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program logs 'ROOT INSERT SUCCESS' and continues processing by reading the next record from the Root Segment input file without any interruption

rules.rule_name: Duplicate Pending Authorization Summary Record Handling
rules.rule_description: When a Pending Authorization Summary record being inserted already exists in the database, the program treats this as a non-critical condition, logs the duplicate occurrence, and continues processing the remaining records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Log: Root Segment
Already Exists in Database
Continue to Next Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: An insert operation has been performed for a Pending Authorization Summary record into the IMS database
acceptance_criteria.When: The database insert operation returns a duplicate key status (status code 'II'), indicating the Pending Authorization Summary record already exists in the database
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program logs 'ROOT SEGMENT ALREADY IN DB' to indicate the duplicate condition, does NOT treat this as an error, and continues processing by reading the next record from the Root Segment input file

rules.rule_name: Failed Insertion of Pending Authorization Summary Record Terminates Program
rules.rule_description: When a Pending Authorization Summary record fails to insert into the database for any reason other than a duplicate, the program logs the failure and immediately terminates with an abnormal return code.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Log: Root Insert Failed
with Status Code
Terminate Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: An insert operation has been performed for a Pending Authorization Summary record into the IMS database
acceptance_criteria.When: The database insert operation returns a status that is neither successful (blank/spaces) nor a duplicate (status code 'II'), indicating an unexpected insert failure
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program logs 'ROOT INSERT FAILED' along with the specific failure status code, immediately stops all further processing, sets the return code to 16, and terminates the program abnormally

acceptance_criteria.Then: If the closure was successful, the program ends all file closure activities; if the closure failed, an error message 'ERROR IN CLOSING 2ND FILE:' along with the specific closure error status is logged, and the program ends all file closure activities

rules.rule_name: Sequential File Closure Order: Root Before Child
rules.rule_description: The Root Segment input file (INFILE1) must always be closed before the Child Segment input file (INFILE2), regardless of whether the Root Segment file closure succeeds or encounters an error.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Close Root Segment File
INFILE1

acceptance_criteria.Given: Both the Root Segment input file (INFILE1) and the Child Segment input file (INFILE2) are open and all records have been processed
acceptance_criteria.When: The file closure sequence is initiated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Root Segment input file (INFILE1) is always closed first, followed by the Child Segment input file (INFILE2), and this order is maintained even if the Root Segment file closure encounters an error

key_functionalities.title: Abnormal Program Termination
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Critical Error Detected])
    B[Display Abort Message:\n'IMS LOAD ABENDING...']
    C[Set Return Code to 16\nIndicating Critical Failure]
    D([Terminate Program])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D

rules.rule_name: Display Abort Message on Critical Processing Failure
rules.rule_description: When a critical error is detected during any stage of the Pending Authorization data load process (file open failure, root segment insert failure, parent segment lookup failure, or child segment insert failure), the system must immediately display an abort notification message to signal that the IMS load operation is terminating abnormally.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Abort Message: 'IMS LOAD ABENDING...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The IMS Pending Authorization load program (PAUDBLOD) is executing AND a critical error has been detected during one of the following stages: (1) opening the Root Segment File or Child Segment File, (2) inserting a Pending Authorization Summary (root) record where the failure is not a duplicate, (3) locating a parent Pending Authorization Summary record during child processing, or (4) inserting a Pending Authorization Detail (child) record where the failure is not a duplicate
acceptance_criteria.When: The program invokes the abnormal termination routine (9999-ABEND) in response to the detected critical error
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must display the abort notification message 'IMS LOAD ABENDING ...' to signal that the IMS Pending Authorization data load is terminating abnormally before any further termination steps are taken

rules.rule_name: Set Critical Failure Return Code on Abnormal Program Termination
rules.rule_description: Upon detecting a critical error during the Pending Authorization data load, after displaying the abort message, the system must set the program return code to 16 to formally indicate a critical failure to any downstream scheduling or monitoring process that invoked this load program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Return Code to 16
Indicating Critical Failure

acceptance_criteria.Given: The IMS Pending Authorization load program (PAUDBLOD) has detected a critical error AND the abort notification message 'IMS LOAD ABENDING ...' has already been displayed
acceptance_criteria.When: The abnormal termination routine continues execution after displaying the abort message
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the program return code to 16, indicating a critical failure status, so that any calling process, job scheduler, or monitoring system is notified that the Pending Authorization data load did not complete successfully

rules.rule_name: Terminate Program Immediately After Critical Failure
rules.rule_description: After displaying the abort message and setting the critical failure return code of 16, the Pending Authorization load program must immediately terminate all processing without executing any further business logic, ensuring no partial or inconsistent data operations continue after a critical failure.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Terminate Program

acceptance_criteria.Given: The IMS Pending Authorization load program (PAUDBLOD) has detected a critical error AND the abort message 'IMS LOAD ABENDING ...' has been displayed AND the return code has been set to 16
acceptance_criteria.When: The abnormal termination routine completes the return code assignment
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must immediately terminate all processing and return control to the calling environment with return code 16, ensuring that no further Pending Authorization Summary or Pending Authorization Detail records are processed, no additional database operations are attempted, and the program exits in a controlled abnormal state

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The PAUDBLOD program has been started and both the Root Segment File (INFILE1) and the Child Segment File (INFILE2) are available for processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes by capturing the current date and attempting to open both input files
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current processing date is captured and displayed; both the Root Segment File and the Child Segment File are successfully opened for reading, and processing continues to the root segment loading phase

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Initialization and File Opening
all_rules.Rule_Description: At program startup, the system captures and displays the current processing date, then opens both the Root Segment File (INFILE1) and the Child Segment File (INFILE2) required for the IMS database load.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The PAUDBLOD program has been started and is attempting to open the Root Segment File (INFILE1) or the Child Segment File (INFILE2)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Either file fails to open successfully (file open status is not blank or '00')
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An error message is displayed identifying which file failed to open along with its error status, and the program terminates abnormally with return code 16

all_rules.Rule_Name: File Open Failure Terminates Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: If either the Root Segment File or the Child Segment File cannot be opened successfully at program startup, the program must terminate immediately with an error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Root Segment File (INFILE1) has been successfully opened and contains Pending Authorization Summary records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reads each record sequentially from the Root Segment File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Each successfully read record is moved into the PENDING-AUTH-SUMMARY structure and passed for insertion into the IMS database; when end-of-file is reached, the program transitions to processing the Child Segment File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential Reading of Root Segment Records
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program reads all Pending Authorization Summary records sequentially from the Root Segment File one at a time, continuing until all records have been processed and end-of-file is reached.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Summary record has been successfully read from the Root Segment File and loaded into the PENDING-AUTH-SUMMARY structure
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program performs an IMS INSERT (ISRT) call using the root unqualified SSA to insert the record as a PAUTSUM0 root segment in the IMS database
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Pending Authorization Summary record is inserted as a root segment into the IMS database, and the program logs a success message and continues reading the next root record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Insert Pending Authorization Summary as Root Segment
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each Pending Authorization Summary record read from the Root Segment File is inserted into the IMS database as a root segment (PAUTSUM0) using an unqualified SSA insert call.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An IMS INSERT call has been made for a Pending Authorization Summary root segment (PAUTSUM0)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The IMS INSERT call returns a successful status (blank status code)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A success message 'ROOT INSERT SUCCESS' is displayed and the program continues to read and process the next root segment record from the Root Segment File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Successful Root Segment Insert
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Summary root segment is successfully inserted into the IMS database, the program logs the success and continues processing the next root record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An IMS INSERT call has been made for a Pending Authorization Summary root segment (PAUTSUM0)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The IMS INSERT call returns a duplicate key status (status code 'II'), indicating the root segment already exists in the database
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A message 'ROOT SEGMENT ALREADY IN DB' is displayed, no error is raised, and the program continues to read and process the next root segment record from the Root Segment File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Duplicate Root Segment
all_rules.Rule_Description: If a Pending Authorization Summary record being inserted already exists in the IMS database, the duplicate is acknowledged and processing continues without error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An IMS INSERT call has been made for a Pending Authorization Summary root segment (PAUTSUM0)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The IMS INSERT call returns a status that is neither successful (blank) nor a duplicate key ('II'), indicating an unexpected insert failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A failure message 'ROOT INSERT FAILED' along with the IMS status code is displayed, and the program terminates abnormally with return code 16

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Root Segment Insert Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: If a Pending Authorization Summary root segment insert fails for any reason other than a duplicate, the program logs the failure and terminates immediately.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All root segment records have been fully processed and the Child Segment File (INFILE2) has been successfully opened and contains Pending Authorization Detail records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reads each record sequentially from the Child Segment File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Each successfully read record is evaluated for a valid numeric Account ID; when end-of-file is reached, the program transitions to the file close phase

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential Reading of Child Segment Records
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all root segments have been loaded, the program reads all Pending Authorization Detail records sequentially from the Child Segment File one at a time, continuing until all records have been processed and end-of-file is reached.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail record has been successfully read from the Child Segment File (INFILE2)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates whether the ROOT-SEG-KEY (Account ID) field in the child record contains a valid numeric value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Account ID is numeric, the record is passed for parent lookup and child insertion; if the Account ID is not numeric, the record is silently skipped and the program reads the next child record without logging any error or warning

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Child Segment Account ID is Numeric
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before processing a child segment record, the Account ID (ROOT-SEG-KEY) must be validated as numeric. Records with non-numeric Account IDs are silently skipped without error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail record with a valid numeric Account ID has been read from the Child Segment File, and the Account ID has been moved to the qualified SSA key value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program performs an IMS GET UNIQUE (GU) call using the qualified root SSA with the Account ID to locate the parent PAUTSUM0 root segment in the IMS database
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the parent root segment is found (blank status), the program proceeds to insert the child segment; if the parent is not found or the lookup fails, the program logs the failure and terminates abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Locate Parent Root Segment Before Child Insert
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before inserting a Pending Authorization Detail child segment, the program must verify that the corresponding parent Pending Authorization Summary root segment exists in the IMS database by performing a qualified Get Unique lookup using the Account ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An IMS GET UNIQUE (GU) call has been made to locate the parent PAUTSUM0 root segment using the Account ID from the child record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The GU call returns a status that is not successful (not blank), indicating the parent root segment was not found or the lookup failed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A failure message 'ROOT GU CALL FAIL' along with the IMS status code and the key feedback area (PAUT-KEYFB) is displayed, and the program terminates abnormally with return code 16

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Root Segment Not Found for Child Insert
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the parent Pending Authorization Summary root segment cannot be located in the IMS database when attempting to insert a child detail record, the program logs the failure details and terminates immediately.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The parent PAUTSUM0 root segment has been successfully located in the IMS database using the Account ID, and the child record data has been loaded into the PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS structure
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program performs an IMS INSERT (ISRT) call using the child unqualified SSA to insert the record as a PAUTDTL1 child segment under the parent root segment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Pending Authorization Detail record is inserted as a child segment under the correct parent in the IMS database, and the program logs a success message and continues reading the next child record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Insert Pending Authorization Detail as Child Segment
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the parent root segment is confirmed to exist, the Pending Authorization Detail record is inserted into the IMS database as a child segment (PAUTDTL1) under the located parent root segment.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An IMS INSERT call has been made for a Pending Authorization Detail child segment (PAUTDTL1) under its parent root segment
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The IMS INSERT call returns a duplicate key status (status code 'II'), indicating the child segment already exists under the parent in the database
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A message 'CHILD SEGMENT ALREADY IN DB' is displayed, no error is raised, and the program continues to read and process the next child segment record from the Child Segment File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Duplicate Child Segment
all_rules.Rule_Description: If a Pending Authorization Detail child segment being inserted already exists in the IMS database under its parent, the duplicate is acknowledged and processing continues without error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An IMS INSERT call has been made for a Pending Authorization Detail child segment (PAUTDTL1) under its parent root segment
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The IMS INSERT call returns a status that is neither successful (blank) nor a duplicate key ('II'), indicating an unexpected insert failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A failure message 'INSERT CALL FAIL FOR CHILD' along with the IMS status code and the key feedback area (PAUT-KEYFB) is displayed, and the program terminates abnormally with return code 16

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Child Segment Insert Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: If a Pending Authorization Detail child segment insert fails for any reason other than a duplicate, the program logs the failure details including the key feedback area and terminates immediately.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All records from both the Root Segment File (INFILE1) and the Child Segment File (INFILE2) have been fully processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program closes both the Root Segment File and the Child Segment File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Both files are closed successfully; if any file fails to close, an error message identifying the file and its error status is displayed, and the program proceeds to normal completion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Input Files After Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all root and child segment records have been fully processed, both input files are closed and any file close errors are logged.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A critical failure has occurred during program execution, such as a file open error, a root segment insert failure, a parent segment not found condition, or a child segment insert failure
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program invokes the abnormal termination routine (9999-ABEND)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message 'IMS LOAD ABENDING ...' is displayed, the program return code is set to 16 to signal abnormal termination, and the program exits immediately without further processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Abnormal Program Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When any critical processing failure occurs during the IMS load, the program terminates abnormally with a standardized error return code to signal failure to any calling or scheduling process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The PAUDBLOD program has been initialized and both input files are open
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins its processing sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All records from the Root Segment File are read and inserted into the IMS database first; only after the Root Segment File is fully exhausted (end-of-file reached) does the program begin reading and processing records from the Child Segment File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Root Segments Must Be Fully Loaded Before Child Segments
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program enforces a strict sequential processing order where all Pending Authorization Summary root segments must be completely loaded into the IMS database before any Pending Authorization Detail child segments are processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The PAUDBLOD program has been invoked and is beginning its initialization phase
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program starts execution
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must capture the current calendar date and the current Julian day-of-year, display a separator line, and display today's date in the processing log before any file operations begin

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture and Display Program Start Date
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the start of program initialization, the program captures the current calendar date and Julian date, then displays the current date to the processing log to record when the IMS load run was initiated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has completed capturing and displaying the current date during initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Root Segment input file (INFILE1) containing Pending Authorization Summary records
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Root Segment input file must be opened successfully in read-only (INPUT) mode so that Pending Authorization Summary records can be read for database loading

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Root Segment Input File for Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: During initialization, the program must open the Root Segment input file (INFILE1), which contains Pending Authorization Summary records, before any root segment data can be read and loaded into the database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the Root Segment input file (INFILE1) containing Pending Authorization Summary records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file open status is evaluated — the file open is considered successful when the status is blank or '00', and unsuccessful for any other status value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file opened successfully, the program proceeds to open the Child Segment input file; if the file failed to open, the program logs the error message 'ERROR IN OPENING INFILE1' along with the file status code, and immediately terminates abnormally with a return code of 16

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Successful Opening of Root Segment File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to open the Root Segment input file, the program validates whether the file was opened successfully. If the file cannot be opened, the program logs an error and terminates abnormally, preventing any further processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Root Segment input file (INFILE1) has been successfully opened and the program is continuing initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the Child Segment input file (INFILE2) containing Pending Authorization Detail records
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Child Segment input file must be opened successfully in read-only (INPUT) mode so that Pending Authorization Detail records can be read for database loading

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Child Segment Input File for Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully opening the Root Segment input file, the program must also open the Child Segment input file (INFILE2), which contains Pending Authorization Detail records, before any child segment data can be read and loaded into the database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to open the Child Segment input file (INFILE2) containing Pending Authorization Detail records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file open status is evaluated — the file open is considered successful when the status is blank or '00', and unsuccessful for any other status value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file opened successfully, the program proceeds to the next phase of processing (reading Root Segment records); if the file failed to open, the program logs the error message 'ERROR IN OPENING INFILE2' along with the file status code, and immediately terminates abnormally with a return code of 16

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Successful Opening of Child Segment File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to open the Child Segment input file, the program validates whether the file was opened successfully. If the file cannot be opened, the program logs an error and terminates abnormally, preventing any further processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is in its initialization phase and needs to prepare for loading Pending Authorization Summary and Pending Authorization Detail records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program completes the initialization sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Root Segment input file (INFILE1) must be opened first, followed by the Child Segment input file (INFILE2); only after both files are confirmed open and ready may the program proceed to read and process Root Segment records; if either file fails to open, the program must not proceed to any data loading activity

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enforce Sequential File Opening Order During Initialization
all_rules.Rule_Description: Both the Root Segment input file and the Child Segment input file must be opened successfully and in a specific sequence — Root Segment file first, then Child Segment file — before any data loading activity can begin. Processing cannot proceed unless both files are available.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A critical failure has occurred during program initialization, such as the inability to open the Root Segment input file (INFILE1) or the Child Segment input file (INFILE2)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The abnormal termination routine is invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must display the message 'IMS LOAD ABENDING', set the program return code to 16 to signal a hard failure to any calling or scheduling process, and immediately stop all further processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Abnormal Program Termination on Initialization Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: If any critical failure occurs during program initialization — specifically the failure to open either input file — the program must terminate abnormally, log the termination, and signal failure to the calling process by setting a return code of 16.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Root Segment input file (INFILE1) has been successfully opened and contains Pending Authorization Summary records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reads the next available record from the Root Segment input file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The record is made available for further processing as a Pending Authorization Summary record, and the program continues to read subsequent records until the end of the file is reached

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential Reading of Pending Authorization Summary Records
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each Pending Authorization Summary record is read sequentially from the Root Segment input file one at a time, and processing continues until all records have been read.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A record has been successfully read from the Root Segment input file (INFILE1)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The record read status confirms the record is available and valid
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The entire record content from INFILE1 is mapped to the Pending Authorization Summary (PENDING-AUTH-SUMMARY) data structure, making it ready for database insertion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Root Segment Record to Pending Authorization Summary
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a root segment record is successfully read from the input file, its data is mapped to the Pending Authorization Summary structure before being inserted into the database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Summary record has been successfully mapped from the Root Segment input file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program invokes the IMS database insert operation for the Pending Authorization Summary segment (PAUTSUM0) using the root unqualified segment search argument
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Pending Authorization Summary record is submitted for insertion into the IMS database as a root-level segment, and the resulting insert status is captured for further evaluation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Insert Pending Authorization Summary Record into Database
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each Pending Authorization Summary record mapped from the input file must be inserted into the IMS database as a root segment (PAUTSUM0) using an unqualified segment search argument.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An insert operation has been performed for a Pending Authorization Summary record into the IMS database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database insert operation returns a successful status (blank/spaces status code)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program logs 'ROOT INSERT SUCCESS' and continues processing by reading the next record from the Root Segment input file without any interruption

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Insertion of Pending Authorization Summary Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Summary record is successfully inserted into the database, the program logs the success and proceeds to read and process the next record from the input file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An insert operation has been performed for a Pending Authorization Summary record into the IMS database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database insert operation returns a duplicate key status (status code 'II'), indicating the Pending Authorization Summary record already exists in the database
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program logs 'ROOT SEGMENT ALREADY IN DB' to indicate the duplicate condition, does NOT treat this as an error, and continues processing by reading the next record from the Root Segment input file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Duplicate Pending Authorization Summary Record Handling
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Summary record being inserted already exists in the database, the program treats this as a non-critical condition, logs the duplicate occurrence, and continues processing the remaining records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An insert operation has been performed for a Pending Authorization Summary record into the IMS database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database insert operation returns a status that is neither successful (blank/spaces) nor a duplicate (status code 'II'), indicating an unexpected insert failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program logs 'ROOT INSERT FAILED' along with the specific failure status code, immediately stops all further processing, sets the return code to 16, and terminates the program abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Failed Insertion of Pending Authorization Summary Record Terminates Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Summary record fails to insert into the database for any reason other than a duplicate, the program logs the failure and immediately terminates with an abnormal return code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is sequentially reading records from the Root Segment input file (INFILE1)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read operation returns an end-of-file status (status code '10'), indicating no more records are available in the Root Segment input file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program sets the end-of-file indicator (END-ROOT-SEG-FILE) to 'Y', stops reading from the Root Segment input file, and concludes the root segment loading phase, allowing the program to proceed to child segment processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: End-of-File Detection for Root Segment Input File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When all Pending Authorization Summary records have been read from the Root Segment input file, the end-of-file condition is detected and the root segment loading phase is concluded.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Summary record (PENDING-AUTH-SUMMARY) has been successfully read from the root segment input file (INFILE1) and is ready for database loading
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program invokes the IMS insert operation (ISRT call) targeting the root summary segment (PAUTSUM0) using an unqualified SSA with the Pending Authorization Summary data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Pending Authorization Summary record is submitted to the IMS database as a root segment entry under the PAUTSUM0 segment definition, and the result of the insert operation is captured for further evaluation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Insert Pending Authorization Summary as Root Segment into IMS Database
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each Pending Authorization Summary record read from the root segment input file, the program invokes the IMS database insert operation to load it as a root (parent) summary segment (PAUTSUM0) using an unqualified Segment Search Argument (SSA), meaning no key qualification is applied during the insert.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The IMS insert operation for the Pending Authorization Summary root segment has been executed and a result status has been returned
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the IMS result status code returned from the insert operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program routes to one of three outcomes: (1) if the status indicates success, log success and continue to the next root record; (2) if the status indicates a duplicate record already exists, log the duplicate and continue to the next root record; (3) if the status indicates any other failure condition, log the failure and trigger abnormal program termination with return code 16

all_rules.Rule_Name: Evaluate Outcome of Root Segment Insert Operation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to insert the Pending Authorization Summary root segment into the IMS database, the program evaluates the result status to determine whether the insert was successful, the record already exists as a duplicate, or an unexpected failure occurred — and routes processing accordingly.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The IMS insert operation for the Pending Authorization Summary root segment has been executed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The IMS result status indicates a successful insert (status is blank/spaces, meaning no error condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program logs 'ROOT INSERT SUCCESS' and returns control to read and process the next root segment record from the input file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Acknowledge Successful Root Segment Insert and Continue Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the IMS database confirms that the Pending Authorization Summary root segment was inserted successfully, the program logs the success and continues processing the next root segment record without interruption.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The IMS insert operation for the Pending Authorization Summary root segment has been executed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The IMS result status indicates the record already exists in the database (duplicate insert condition, status code 'II')
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program logs 'ROOT SEGMENT ALREADY IN DB', does NOT treat this as a failure, and returns control to read and process the next root segment record — the duplicate record is skipped without any abnormal termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Duplicate Pending Authorization Summary Record Gracefully
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the IMS database reports that the Pending Authorization Summary root segment being inserted already exists in the database (duplicate), the program treats this as a non-critical condition, logs the occurrence, and continues processing the remaining root segment records without stopping.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The IMS insert operation for the Pending Authorization Summary root segment has been executed and the result status is neither a success (blank) nor a duplicate record condition ('II')
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The IMS result status indicates an unexpected failure — any status other than blank (success) or 'II' (duplicate)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program logs 'ROOT INSERT FAILED' along with the specific failure status code received, then triggers abnormal termination by logging 'IMS LOAD ABENDING', setting the program return code to 16, and immediately stopping all processing — no further root or child records are processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Abnormal Termination on Root Segment Insert Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the IMS database returns an unexpected failure status (neither success nor duplicate) during the insert of a Pending Authorization Summary root segment, the program logs the failure condition and immediately triggers abnormal program termination, halting all further processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Summary record has been read from the Root Segment input file and an insert operation has been attempted against the IMS database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database insert operation returns a status indicating that the Pending Authorization Summary record already exists in the database (duplicate key condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system identifies the insert outcome as a duplicate and does not treat it as a failure — processing continues to the next root segment record without aborting

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Duplicate Root Segment During Database Insert
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Summary (root segment) is being loaded into the database, the system must detect whether the record already exists. If a duplicate is found, processing must continue without interruption.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Summary record insert has been attempted and the database has returned a duplicate key status indicating the record already exists
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The duplicate key condition is confirmed for the root segment insert
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system logs the message 'ROOT SEGMENT ALREADY IN DB' to indicate the Pending Authorization Summary record was already present, and then continues processing the next root segment record without stopping or raising an error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Log Duplicate Root Segment Already Present in Database
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Summary record is found to already exist in the database during the load process, the system must log an informational message indicating the duplicate condition before continuing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Summary record insert has been attempted and the result was either a successful insert or a duplicate key condition
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The insert outcome is either a success (record newly inserted) or a duplicate (record already existed in the database)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system continues to the next root segment record from the input file without any interruption, ensuring that neither a successful insert nor a duplicate condition causes the load process to stop — only an insert failure for a reason other than a duplicate will cause the process to abort with a failure return code of 16

all_rules.Rule_Name: Continue Processing After Duplicate Root Segment Detection
all_rules.Rule_Description: A duplicate Pending Authorization Summary record in the database is a tolerated condition. The program must not abort and must proceed to process the next available root segment record from the input file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Summary record has been successfully read from the Root Segment input file and its data has been mapped to the Pending Authorization Summary structure
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the insert operation to load the Pending Authorization Summary record as a root segment into the IMS database using an unqualified segment search argument
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The database insert operation is executed for the Pending Authorization Summary record, and the resulting status is captured for subsequent evaluation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invoke Pending Authorization Summary Insert into Database
all_rules.Rule_Description: When processing each Pending Authorization Summary record from the input file, the system must invoke the database insert operation to load the record as a root (parent) segment in the IMS database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Summary record insert operation has been executed against the IMS database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the database operation status returned after the insert attempt
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the status is blank (indicating success), the system logs 'ROOT INSERT SUCCESS' and continues to process the next record; if the status is not blank, the system proceeds to determine whether the failure is due to a duplicate record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Evaluate Success of Pending Authorization Summary Insert
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to insert a Pending Authorization Summary record into the database, the system must evaluate whether the insert operation completed successfully by checking the database operation status.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Summary record insert operation has returned a non-success status from the IMS database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the database operation status indicates a duplicate record condition (status = 'II', meaning the record already exists in the database)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the status is 'II' (duplicate), the system logs 'ROOT SEGMENT ALREADY IN DB' and continues processing the next record without treating it as an error; if the status is any value other than blank or 'II', the system proceeds to log the failure and terminate

all_rules.Rule_Name: Identify Duplicate Pending Authorization Summary Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Summary insert does not succeed, the system must determine whether the failure is because the record already exists in the database (duplicate), in order to decide whether to continue processing or terminate.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Summary record insert operation has returned a status that is neither blank (success) nor 'II' (duplicate)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system identifies that the insert has failed due to an unexpected or unrecoverable database condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the message 'ROOT INSERT FAILED' along with the specific database status code returned, providing a traceable record of the failure reason before initiating program termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Log Pending Authorization Summary Insert Failure Reason
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Summary record fails to insert into the database for a reason other than a duplicate, the system must record and display the specific failure reason to support investigation and audit.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Summary record insert has failed with a status that is neither blank (success) nor 'II' (duplicate), and the failure reason has been logged
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines that the insert failure is unrecoverable and no further processing should occur
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the message 'IMS LOAD ABENDING', sets the program return code to 16 to signal a hard failure to the calling or scheduling process, and immediately ends the program — no further records from either the Root Segment file or the Child Segment file are processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Program on Unrecoverable Pending Authorization Summary Insert Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Summary record fails to insert into the database for any reason other than a duplicate, the program must immediately stop all processing, signal a hard failure to the calling environment, and terminate.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Summary record insert operation has been executed and the database status is either blank (successful insert) or 'II' (record already exists as a duplicate)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms that the insert outcome is either a success or an acceptable duplicate condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system continues to the next iteration of the Root Segment file processing loop, reading and attempting to insert the next Pending Authorization Summary record without any interruption or error escalation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Continue Processing After Successful or Duplicate Root Segment Insert
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Summary record is either successfully inserted or found to already exist in the database, the program must continue processing the remaining records in the Root Segment input file without interruption.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Child Segment input file (INFILE2) has been successfully opened and is ready for reading, and the end-of-file indicator (END-CHILD-SEG-FILE) is not yet set to 'Y'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program requests the next sequential record from the Child Segment file (INFILE2)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program reads the next available record from INFILE2 and proceeds to evaluate whether the read was successful, continuing this loop until the end-of-file condition is reached

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential Reading of Child Segment Records Until End-of-File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program reads child segment records one at a time from the Child Segment input file (INFILE2) in a continuous loop until all records have been processed and end-of-file is reached.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the Child Segment file (INFILE2)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file status returned is blank (spaces) or '00', indicating a successful read
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program treats the record as successfully retrieved and proceeds to validate the Account ID (ROOT-SEG-KEY) for numeric content before any further processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Child Segment Record Read Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each read attempt from the Child Segment file, the program determines whether the record was successfully retrieved by evaluating the file status, and routes processing accordingly.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A child segment record has been successfully read from INFILE2
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates whether the Account ID (ROOT-SEG-KEY) field in the record contains a valid numeric value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Account ID is numeric, the program proceeds to prepare the child record for database insertion; if the Account ID is NOT numeric, the record is silently skipped and the program immediately reads the next record from INFILE2 without logging any error or warning

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account ID Numeric Validation for Child Segment Records
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before a child segment record can be processed and inserted into the database, the Account ID (ROOT-SEG-KEY) extracted from the record must be validated to ensure it contains only numeric characters, as it serves as the key linking the child record to its parent.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A child segment record has been successfully read from INFILE2 and the Account ID (ROOT-SEG-KEY) has been confirmed as numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares the child record for database processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID (ROOT-SEG-KEY) is moved into the qualified SSA key value (QUAL-SSA-KEY-VALUE) to be used as the lookup key for finding the parent record, and the child record data (CHILD-SEG-REC) is moved into the Pending Authorization Details structure (PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS) ready for database insertion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare Child Record for Database Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a child segment record passes the Account ID numeric validation, the program prepares the record for database insertion by setting the Account ID as the qualified lookup key to locate the parent Pending Authorization Summary record, and staging the child record data in the Pending Authorization Details structure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The child segment record has been prepared with the Account ID set as the lookup key and the record data staged in PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program is ready to persist the child record into the database
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program invokes the child segment insert processing routine (3100-INSERT-CHILD-SEG) which handles parent record lookup and child record insertion into the IMS database

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invoke Child Segment Database Insert Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the child record is prepared with a valid numeric Account ID and staged in the Pending Authorization Details structure, the program invokes the child segment insert processing routine to locate the parent record and insert the child into the database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation on the Child Segment file (INFILE2) did not return a successful record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the file status to determine the nature of the read issue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file status is '10' (end-of-file), the program sets the end-of-file indicator (END-CHILD-SEG-FILE) to 'Y', which terminates the read loop and signals that all child segment records have been processed; if the file status is any other value, the program treats it as a read error and logs an error message before attempting to read the next record

all_rules.Rule_Name: End-of-File Detection for Child Segment File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a read from the Child Segment file does not return a successful record, the program determines whether the condition is a normal end-of-file or an unexpected read error, and routes processing accordingly.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation on the Child Segment file (INFILE2) has returned a status that is neither successful (spaces or '00') nor end-of-file ('10')
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program identifies an unexpected read error condition on the Child Segment file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program displays the message 'ERROR READING CHILD SEG INFILE' to log the read failure, and then continues by attempting to read the next record from INFILE2 without terminating the program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Log Child Segment File Read Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected error occurs while reading from the Child Segment file (neither a successful read nor an end-of-file condition), the program logs an error message to notify of the read failure, and continues attempting to read subsequent records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The read operation on the Child Segment file (INFILE2) has returned an end-of-file status ('10')
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sets the end-of-file indicator (END-CHILD-SEG-FILE) to 'Y'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The read loop for child segment records terminates, all child segment records from INFILE2 have been processed, and the program proceeds to the file close phase

all_rules.Rule_Name: Termination of Child Segment Processing Upon End-of-File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the end-of-file condition is detected on the Child Segment file, the program marks the completion of child segment record processing and exits the read loop, signaling that all available child records have been handled.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail record has been successfully read from the Child Segment File (INFILE2)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID (ROOT-SEG-KEY) associated with the child record is evaluated for numeric validity
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Account ID is numeric, the record is accepted for further processing; if the Account ID is not numeric, the record is silently skipped and no insert is performed for that record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Account ID is Numeric Before Child Record Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each successfully read Pending Authorization Detail (child segment) record, the Account ID (root segment key) must be validated as a numeric value before the record is eligible for database insertion. Records with non-numeric Account IDs are excluded from processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail record has been successfully read from the Child Segment File (INFILE2) and the Account ID (ROOT-SEG-KEY) has been confirmed as numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the child record for database insertion
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID (ROOT-SEG-KEY) is set as the qualified lookup key (QUAL-SSA-KEY-VALUE) to identify the parent Pending Authorization Summary record, and the child record data (CHILD-SEG-REC) is loaded into the Pending Authorization Details processing structure (PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prepare Child Segment Record for Database Insert When Account ID is Valid
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Detail record passes the numeric Account ID validation, the Account ID is set as the lookup key to locate the parent Pending Authorization Summary record, and the child record data is loaded into the processing structure in preparation for database insertion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail record has passed numeric Account ID validation and has been prepared with the lookup key and child record data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The child record is ready for database insertion
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system invokes the parent root segment location and child segment insert process (3100-INSERT-CHILD-SEG) to verify the parent Pending Authorization Summary exists and insert the child Pending Authorization Detail record into the database

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invoke Parent Lookup and Child Insert Process for Valid Child Records
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a Pending Authorization Detail record is prepared with a valid numeric Account ID and its data is loaded, the system invokes the parent root segment location and child segment insertion process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail record has been successfully read from the Child Segment File (INFILE2)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID (ROOT-SEG-KEY) is found to be non-numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The record is skipped entirely — no lookup key is set, no child record data is loaded, no database insert is attempted, no error message is generated, and the program continues reading the next record from the Child Segment File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Child Record When Account ID is Non-Numeric
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Detail record contains a non-numeric Account ID, the record is silently bypassed — no insert is attempted, no error is raised, and processing continues with the next record in the Child Segment File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is about to perform a lookup for the parent Pending Authorization Summary (PAUTSUM0) root segment in the IMS database using the account ID from the child segment record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The child segment record has been successfully read and its account ID (ROOT-SEG-KEY) has been confirmed as numeric
