Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The database status indicator (PAUT-PCB-STATUS) must be cleared and reset to its initial empty state before the parent lookup is executed, ensuring no residual status from any prior database operation influences the outcome of the parent search

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Previous Database Status Before Parent Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before performing a lookup for the parent Pending Authorization Summary record, any previously held database status must be cleared to ensure the result of the upcoming lookup is not influenced by prior operations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail (child) record has been read from the child segment input file, its account ID (ROOT-SEG-KEY) has been validated as numeric, and the account ID has been set as the qualified search key (QUAL-SSA-KEY-VALUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system invokes the IMS database lookup service (CBLTDLI) with a Get Unique (GU) function using the qualified search key (ROOT-QUAL-SSA) to search for the parent Pending Authorization Summary (PAUTSUM0) segment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The IMS database returns the lookup result: either the parent Pending Authorization Summary record is located and the database status is blank (success), or the parent is not found and the database status contains a non-blank value indicating failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Locate Parent Pending Authorization Summary Using Account ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: To insert a Pending Authorization Detail (child) record, the system must first locate the corresponding parent Pending Authorization Summary (PAUTSUM0) record in the IMS database using a qualified search by account ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A qualified Get Unique (GU) lookup has been performed against the IMS database to locate the parent Pending Authorization Summary (PAUTSUM0) record using the account ID from the child segment record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database status returned from the GU lookup is blank, confirming that the parent Pending Authorization Summary record was successfully found
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system logs a success message ('GU CALL TO ROOT SEG SUCCESS') and proceeds to execute the child segment insert operation (3200-INSERT-IMS-CALL) to insert the Pending Authorization Detail record under the located parent

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Child Insert When Parent Pending Authorization Summary Is Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the parent Pending Authorization Summary record is successfully located in the IMS database, the program is authorized to proceed with inserting the corresponding Pending Authorization Detail (child) record under that parent.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A qualified Get Unique (GU) lookup has been performed against the IMS database to locate the parent Pending Authorization Summary (PAUTSUM0) record using the account ID from the child segment record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database status returned from the GU lookup is not blank AND is not a duplicate indicator ('II'), meaning the parent Pending Authorization Summary record was not found or an unexpected database condition occurred
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) log the failure status code received from the database lookup ('ROOT GU CALL FAIL:' followed by the status value), (2) log the key feedback area details from the child segment ('KFB AREA IN CHILD:' followed by PAUT-KEYFB) to assist in identifying which record caused the failure, and (3) immediately terminate the entire program with a return code of 16, halting all further processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Program When Parent Pending Authorization Summary Cannot Be Located
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the parent Pending Authorization Summary record cannot be found in the IMS database during the qualified lookup, the program must log the failure details and terminate immediately, as a child Pending Authorization Detail record cannot exist without a valid parent.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail record has been read from the Child Segment File and its Account ID (ROOT-SEG-KEY) has been validated as numeric and set as the qualified lookup key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to locate the parent Pending Authorization Summary record in the database using the Account ID as the qualified search key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the parent Pending Authorization Summary record from the database if it exists, and the lookup result status is captured for evaluation before any child insert is attempted

all_rules.Rule_Name: Locate Parent Pending Authorization Summary Before Child Insert
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before inserting a Pending Authorization Detail (child) record, the system must perform a qualified lookup to locate the corresponding parent Pending Authorization Summary record in the database using the Account ID from the child record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A lookup has been performed to locate the parent Pending Authorization Summary record in the database using the Account ID from the child record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the result of the parent lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the lookup was successful (status is blank/spaces), the system proceeds to insert the Pending Authorization Detail (child) record; if the lookup failed for any reason other than a duplicate condition, the system logs the failure details and terminates processing with an error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Evaluate Whether Parent Pending Authorization Summary Was Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to locate the parent Pending Authorization Summary record, the system evaluates the lookup result to determine whether to proceed with the child insert or to handle the failure condition.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A lookup was performed to locate the parent Pending Authorization Summary record in the database using the Account ID from the child record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The lookup result status is neither blank/spaces (success) nor a duplicate indicator, meaning the parent Pending Authorization Summary record was not found or an unexpected condition occurred
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system logs the failure status code ('ROOT GU CALL FAIL:' followed by the status value) and logs the key feedback area details ('KFB AREA IN CHILD:' followed by the key feedback value PAUT-KEYFB) to identify which Account ID caused the failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Log Parent Pending Authorization Summary Not Found Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the parent Pending Authorization Summary record cannot be located in the database for a given Account ID, the system must log the failure status and the key feedback area to support investigation of the missing parent record before terminating.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has logged the failure status and key feedback area after failing to locate the parent Pending Authorization Summary record for a child record's Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program invokes the termination routine (9999-ABEND) due to the parent not being found
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the message 'IMS LOAD ABENDING ...', sets the program return code to 16 to signal a hard failure to any calling or scheduling process, and immediately terminates all further processing — no additional records are read or inserted

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Program When Parent Pending Authorization Summary Is Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the parent Pending Authorization Summary record cannot be located in the database for a child record's Account ID, the program must immediately stop all processing and signal a hard failure to the calling process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A lookup was performed to locate the parent Pending Authorization Summary record in the database using the Account ID from the child record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The lookup result status is blank/spaces, confirming the parent Pending Authorization Summary record was successfully found
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system logs 'GU CALL TO ROOT SEG SUCCESS' and proceeds to execute the child segment insert routine (3200-INSERT-IMS-CALL) to insert the Pending Authorization Detail record under the located parent

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Insert Child Pending Authorization Detail When Parent Is Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the parent Pending Authorization Summary record is successfully located in the database, the system is authorized to proceed with inserting the corresponding Pending Authorization Detail (child) record under that parent.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail record (PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS) is ready for insertion and the parent Pending Authorization Summary root segment has been successfully located in the IMS database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to insert the Pending Authorization Detail record as a child segment under the located parent root segment in the IMS database using an unqualified SSA
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Pending Authorization Detail record (PAUTDTL1) is submitted for insertion as a child segment under the parent Pending Authorization Summary root segment in the IMS database

all_rules.Rule_Name: Insert Pending Authorization Detail Record Under Parent Summary
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the parent Pending Authorization Summary record has been successfully located in the database, the system must insert the Pending Authorization Detail (child) record (PAUTDTL1) under that parent using an unqualified segment search argument.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to insert a Pending Authorization Detail record (PAUTDTL1) as a child segment under the parent Pending Authorization Summary root segment in the IMS database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The IMS database insert operation completes successfully with no errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system logs the message 'CHILD SEGMENT INSERTED SUCCESS' and returns to continue processing the next child record from the Child Segment File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Insertion of Pending Authorization Detail Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Pending Authorization Detail (child) record is successfully inserted into the IMS database under its parent, the system logs a success confirmation message and continues processing the remaining child records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to insert a Pending Authorization Detail record (PAUTDTL1) as a child segment under the parent Pending Authorization Summary root segment in the IMS database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The IMS database reports that the child segment already exists in the database (duplicate segment condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system logs the message 'CHILD SEGMENT ALREADY IN DB', does NOT treat this as a failure, and returns to continue processing the next child record from the Child Segment File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Duplicate Pending Authorization Detail Record Handling
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Detail (child) record being inserted already exists in the IMS database under the same parent, the system treats this as a non-critical condition, logs the duplicate occurrence, and continues processing remaining child records without stopping.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to insert a Pending Authorization Detail record (PAUTDTL1) as a child segment under the parent Pending Authorization Summary root segment in the IMS database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The IMS database insert operation fails with an error condition that is neither a successful insert nor a duplicate segment condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system logs the failure message 'INSERT CALL FAIL FOR CHILD' along with the specific error status code and the key feedback area (PAUT-KEYFB) to identify the failing record, and then proceeds to abnormal program termination with return code 16

all_rules.Rule_Name: Failed Insertion of Pending Authorization Detail Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the insertion of a Pending Authorization Detail (child) record fails for any reason other than a duplicate, the system logs the failure details including the error status and the key feedback area, then terminates the program abnormally.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The insertion of a Pending Authorization Detail record (PAUTDTL1) into the IMS database has failed with an unrecoverable error (not a duplicate condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system invokes the abnormal termination routine after logging the failure details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system logs 'IMS LOAD ABENDING', sets the program return code to 16 to signal a hard failure to the calling process, and terminates the program immediately without processing any further child records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Abnormal Program Termination on Child Insert Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a critical failure occurs during the insertion of a Pending Authorization Detail record that cannot be recovered from, the program must stop all further processing immediately and signal failure to the calling environment by setting a return code of 16.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail record has been submitted for insertion into the IMS database under its corresponding Pending Authorization Summary (parent) record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The insertion of the Pending Authorization Detail record into the IMS database completes successfully with no errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system logs the message 'CHILD SEGMENT INSERTED SUCCESS' and continues processing the next Pending Authorization Detail record without aborting

all_rules.Rule_Name: Log Success When Pending Authorization Detail Record Is Inserted
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Detail (child) record is successfully inserted into the IMS database, the system logs a success message and continues processing the next child record without any interruption.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail record has been submitted for insertion into the IMS database under its corresponding Pending Authorization Summary (parent) record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The IMS database detects that the Pending Authorization Detail record already exists (duplicate segment detected)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system logs the message 'CHILD SEGMENT ALREADY IN DB' to indicate the record is already present, does not treat this as a failure, does not abort the program, and continues processing the next Pending Authorization Detail record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Duplicate Pending Authorization Detail Record Without Aborting
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Detail (child) record being inserted already exists in the IMS database, the system treats this as a non-critical condition, logs an informational message, and continues processing the remaining child records without stopping the program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail record has been submitted for insertion into the IMS database under its corresponding Pending Authorization Summary (parent) record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The insertion fails with an error condition that is neither a successful insert nor a duplicate record detection
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system logs the message 'INSERT CALL FAIL FOR CHILD' along with the key feedback area details, immediately stops all further processing, and terminates the program with a return code of 16 indicating a hard failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Abort Program on Critical Failure During Pending Authorization Detail Insert
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Detail (child) record fails to insert into the IMS database for any reason other than a duplicate, the system logs the failure details and immediately terminates the entire program with a failure exit code.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail (child) segment insert operation has been attempted into the IMS database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database confirms the insert completed successfully with no errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program logs a success message 'CHILD SEGMENT INSERTED SUCCESS' and continues processing the next child record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Successful Child Segment Insert
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to insert a Pending Authorization Detail (child) record into the database, the program evaluates whether the insert operation completed successfully.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail (child) segment insert operation has been attempted into the IMS database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database indicates the child segment already exists (duplicate condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program logs the message 'CHILD SEGMENT ALREADY IN DB' and continues processing the remaining child records without terminating

all_rules.Rule_Name: Tolerate Duplicate Child Segment Without Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Detail (child) record already exists in the database, the program treats this as an acceptable condition and continues processing without stopping.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail (child) segment insert operation has been attempted into the IMS database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The database returns a status that is neither a successful completion nor a duplicate record condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program identifies this as an unexpected critical failure and proceeds to log the failure details and terminate processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Identify Unexpected Child Segment Insert Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a child segment insert attempt, the program determines whether the failure is an unexpected error — any outcome that is neither a successful insert nor a known duplicate condition — which requires immediate program termination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail (child) segment insert has failed with an unexpected error that is not a duplicate
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program detects the unexpected failure condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program logs the message 'INSERT CALL FAIL FOR CHILD:' along with the specific database status code (PAUT-PCB-STATUS) that caused the failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Log Child Segment Insert Failure Status
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected failure occurs during the insert of a Pending Authorization Detail (child) record, the program captures and logs the specific failure status returned by the database for diagnostic purposes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail (child) segment insert has failed with an unexpected error and the failure status has already been logged
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program is recording diagnostic information about the failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program additionally logs the message 'KFB AREA IN CHILD:' along with the key feedback area (PAUT-KEYFB) to identify the specific child record that caused the failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Log Key Feedback Area for Child Insert Failure Diagnosis
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected failure occurs during the insert of a Pending Authorization Detail (child) record, the program also logs the key feedback area to identify which specific record caused the failure, enabling business investigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail (child) segment insert has failed unexpectedly and all failure details have been logged
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program determines that processing cannot safely continue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program invokes the termination routine which displays the message 'IMS LOAD ABENDING ...' to signal that the IMS load process is being aborted

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Program Termination on Critical Child Insert Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: After logging all diagnostic details for an unexpected child segment insert failure, the program initiates an abnormal termination sequence to prevent further processing of potentially corrupt or incomplete data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program termination routine has been invoked due to a critical failure during Pending Authorization Detail (child) segment insert
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program executes the termination sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program sets the return code to 16 to signal a critical error to calling processes and job schedulers, then terminates abnormally, halting all further Pending Authorization data loading

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Critical Error Return Code and Terminate Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon abnormal termination due to a critical child segment insert failure, the program sets a return code of 16 to communicate the critical failure status to any downstream processes or job schedulers, then terminates.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All Pending Authorization Summary records from the Root Segment input file (INFILE1) have been fully read and processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the Root Segment input file (INFILE1)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Root Segment input file (INFILE1) is closed and released from the program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Root Segment Input File After Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all Pending Authorization Summary (root segment) records have been processed and loaded, the Root Segment input file (INFILE1) must be closed to release it from the program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the Root Segment input file (INFILE1)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file closure status is evaluated — a blank status or status '00' indicates success, any other status indicates a closure failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the closure was successful, processing continues to close the Child Segment file; if the closure failed, an error message 'ERROR IN CLOSING 1ST FILE:' along with the specific closure error status is logged, and processing continues to close the Child Segment file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Root Segment File Closure Success
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to close the Root Segment input file (INFILE1), the program must verify whether the closure was successful. If the closure fails, an error must be logged identifying the Root Segment file as the source of the problem.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Root Segment input file (INFILE1) closure has been attempted and all Pending Authorization Detail (child segment) records from INFILE2 have been fully read and processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initiates the closure of the Child Segment input file (INFILE2)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Child Segment input file (INFILE2) is closed and released from the program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Child Segment Input File After Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the Root Segment input file closure has been attempted (regardless of its outcome), the Child Segment input file (INFILE2) must be closed to release it from the program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to close the Child Segment input file (INFILE2)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file closure status is evaluated — a blank status or status '00' indicates success, any other status indicates a closure failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the closure was successful, the program ends all file closure activities; if the closure failed, an error message 'ERROR IN CLOSING 2ND FILE:' along with the specific closure error status is logged, and the program ends all file closure activities

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Child Segment File Closure Success
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to close the Child Segment input file (INFILE2), the program must verify whether the closure was successful. If the closure fails, an error must be logged identifying the Child Segment file as the source of the problem.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Both the Root Segment input file (INFILE1) and the Child Segment input file (INFILE2) are open and all records have been processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file closure sequence is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Root Segment input file (INFILE1) is always closed first, followed by the Child Segment input file (INFILE2), and this order is maintained even if the Root Segment file closure encounters an error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential File Closure Order: Root Before Child
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Root Segment input file (INFILE1) must always be closed before the Child Segment input file (INFILE2), regardless of whether the Root Segment file closure succeeds or encounters an error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The IMS Pending Authorization load program (PAUDBLOD) is executing AND a critical error has been detected during one of the following stages: (1) opening the Root Segment File or Child Segment File, (2) inserting a Pending Authorization Summary (root) record where the failure is not a duplicate, (3) locating a parent Pending Authorization Summary record during child processing, or (4) inserting a Pending Authorization Detail (child) record where the failure is not a duplicate
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program invokes the abnormal termination routine (9999-ABEND) in response to the detected critical error
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display the abort notification message 'IMS LOAD ABENDING ...' to signal that the IMS Pending Authorization data load is terminating abnormally before any further termination steps are taken

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Abort Message on Critical Processing Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a critical error is detected during any stage of the Pending Authorization data load process (file open failure, root segment insert failure, parent segment lookup failure, or child segment insert failure), the system must immediately display an abort notification message to signal that the IMS load operation is terminating abnormally.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The IMS Pending Authorization load program (PAUDBLOD) has detected a critical error AND the abort notification message 'IMS LOAD ABENDING ...' has already been displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The abnormal termination routine continues execution after displaying the abort message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the program return code to 16, indicating a critical failure status, so that any calling process, job scheduler, or monitoring system is notified that the Pending Authorization data load did not complete successfully

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Critical Failure Return Code on Abnormal Program Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon detecting a critical error during the Pending Authorization data load, after displaying the abort message, the system must set the program return code to 16 to formally indicate a critical failure to any downstream scheduling or monitoring process that invoked this load program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The IMS Pending Authorization load program (PAUDBLOD) has detected a critical error AND the abort message 'IMS LOAD ABENDING ...' has been displayed AND the return code has been set to 16
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The abnormal termination routine completes the return code assignment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must immediately terminate all processing and return control to the calling environment with return code 16, ensuring that no further Pending Authorization Summary or Pending Authorization Detail records are processed, no additional database operations are attempted, and the program exits in a controlled abnormal state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Program Immediately After Critical Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: After displaying the abort message and setting the critical failure return code of 16, the Pending Authorization load program must immediately terminate all processing without executing any further business logic, ensuring no partial or inconsistent data operations continue after a critical failure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Detail record has been read from the child segment file and the Account ID (ROOT-SEG-KEY) has been set as the qualified search key value (QUAL-SSA-KEY-VALUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a qualified Get Unique (GU) lookup against the Pending Authorization Summary segment (PAUTSUM0) in the IMS database using the Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the parent Pending Authorization Summary record that matches the given Account ID, positioning the database cursor on that parent record so that the child detail record can be inserted beneath it

all_rules.Rule_Name: Locate Parent Pending Authorization Summary Record Before Child Insert
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before inserting a Pending Authorization Detail record, the system must first locate the corresponding parent Pending Authorization Summary record in the database using the Account ID as the lookup key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A qualified Get Unique (GU) lookup has been performed against the Pending Authorization Summary segment (PAUTSUM0) using the Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The GU lookup returns a status that is neither successful (blank status) nor a duplicate indicator ('II'), meaning the parent record was not found or an unexpected error occurred
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system logs the GU call failure status code and the Key Feedback Area (PAUT-KEYFB) to identify which Account ID caused the failure, then immediately terminates the entire program with a return code of 16, stopping all further processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Processing When Parent Pending Authorization Summary Record Cannot Be Located
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the parent Pending Authorization Summary record cannot be found or the lookup fails for any reason, the system must log the failure details and immediately stop all processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The parent Pending Authorization Summary record (PAUTSUM0) has been successfully located in the IMS database using the Account ID, and the Pending Authorization Detail data (PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS) is ready for insertion
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs an Insert (ISRT) call to add the Pending Authorization Detail segment (PAUTDTL1) as a child record under the located parent Pending Authorization Summary record, using an unqualified SSA for the child segment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Pending Authorization Detail record is stored in the IMS database as a child of the corresponding Pending Authorization Summary record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Insert Pending Authorization Detail Record Under Located Parent
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the parent Pending Authorization Summary record has been successfully located, the system inserts the Pending Authorization Detail record as a child segment under that parent in the database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An Insert (ISRT) call has been performed to add a Pending Authorization Detail record (PAUTDTL1) under its parent Pending Authorization Summary record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The insert operation returns a successful status (blank status code), indicating the record was newly created in the database
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system logs 'CHILD SEGMENT INSERTED SUCCESS' and continues processing the next child segment record from the input file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Confirm Successful Insertion of Pending Authorization Detail Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Detail record is successfully inserted into the database, the system logs a confirmation message and continues processing the remaining child records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An Insert (ISRT) call has been performed to add a Pending Authorization Detail record (PAUTDTL1) under its parent Pending Authorization Summary record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The insert operation returns a duplicate indicator status ('II'), meaning an identical Pending Authorization Detail record already exists in the database under that parent
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system logs 'CHILD SEGMENT ALREADY IN DB' to record the duplicate occurrence and continues processing the next child segment record from the input file without terminating the program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Allow Continuation When Pending Authorization Detail Record Already Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: If a Pending Authorization Detail record being inserted already exists in the database under the same parent, this is treated as a non-critical condition and processing continues without stopping.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An Insert (ISRT) call has been performed to add a Pending Authorization Detail record (PAUTDTL1) under its parent Pending Authorization Summary record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The insert operation returns a status that is neither successful (blank status) nor a duplicate indicator ('II'), indicating an unexpected failure occurred during the child record insert
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system logs 'INSERT CALL FAIL FOR CHILD' along with the failure status code and the Key Feedback Area (PAUT-KEYFB) to identify the failed record, then immediately terminates the entire program with a return code of 16, stopping all further processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Processing on Unexpected Pending Authorization Detail Insert Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: If a Pending Authorization Detail record fails to insert for any reason other than a duplicate, the system must log the failure details and immediately stop all processing.

description:
PAUDBLOD is a batch IMS load program that reads Pending Authorization Summary (root segments) and Pending Authorization Detail (child segments) from two sequential input files and inserts them into an IMS database. The program first loads all root segments (PAUTSUM0) from INFILE1, then loads all child segments (PAUTDTL1) from INFILE2 by first locating the parent root segment via a qualified Get Unique (GU) call before inserting each child record.
- **Execution Environment**: Batch - **Database Access**: IMS, Sequential Files - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main module (entry point DLITCBL, uses GOBACK, accepts PCB masks via PROCEDURE DIVISION USING)
### Key Functionalities: 1: Program Initialization - Capture the current date and display it, then open the Root Segment input file (INFILE1) and the Child Segment input file (INFILE2) for processing 2: Read Root Segment Records - Sequentially read each record from the Root Segment input file (INFILE1) until end-of-file is reached 3: Insert Root Segment into Database - For each root segment record read, insert it as a root (summary) segment (PAUTSUM0) into the IMS database using an unqualified SSA 4: Handle Duplicate Root Segment - If the root segment already exists in the database (duplicate key), log a message indicating the segment is already present and continue without aborting 5: Handle Root Segment Insert Failure - If the root segment insert fails for any reason other than a duplicate, log the failure status and terminate the program with an error 6: Read Child Segment Records - Sequentially read each record from the Child Segment input file (INFILE2) until end-of-file is reached 7: Validate Child Segment Key - For each child segment record read, verify that the associated root segment key (account ID) is numeric before proceeding with the insert 8: Locate Parent Root Segment - Using the account ID from the child segment record, perform a qualified Get Unique (GU) call to locate the corresponding parent root segment (PAUTSUM0) in the IMS database 9: Handle Root Segment Not Found for Child - If the GU call to locate the parent root segment fails, log the failure status and key feedback area, then terminate the program with an error 10: Insert Child Segment into Database - After successfully locating the parent root segment, insert the child (detail) segment (PAUTDTL1) under the parent in the IMS database using an unqualified SSA 11: Handle Duplicate Child Segment - If the child segment already exists in the database, log a message indicating the segment is already present and continue without aborting 12: Handle Child Segment Insert Failure - If the child segment insert fails for any reason other than a duplicate, log the failure status and key feedback area, then terminate the program with an error 13: Close Input Files - Close both the Root Segment input file (INFILE1) and the Child Segment input file (INFILE2) after all records have been processed, logging any errors encountered during closure 14: Abnormal Program Termination - If a critical error occurs at any stage, display an abort message, set the return code to 16, and terminate the program
